**Core settings**

| Setting | What it is | Values | Default | When to change it | What to expect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `refreshPeriodMs`<br/>Scan interval (ms) | How often the discovery scan runs, in ms. 900000 is 15 minutes. | number, min 60000, max 86400000 | `900000` | Leave at 15 minutes unless you have a reason. Lengthen it if you want a calmer universe that changes less often. | Each scan is a batch of Binance requests, so a very short period burns request weight for little benefit — the filters below work on 24h figures that barely move minute to minute. |
| `blacklist`<br/>Blocklist | Symbols discovery must never auto-add. | text | `[]` | Add a coin the moment you decide you never want it auto-traded — a token you distrust, one you hold elsewhere, or one that has burned you. | Blacklisted symbols are never auto-added, whatever they score. It does not remove a coin you added by hand; unpin or remove that separately. |
| `min24hPairVolumeUsd`<br/>Min 24h volume on this market (USD) | Can the bot get in and out? The 24h trading volume of the exact market it would buy on, in US dollars. Set this low: a coin can be hugely popular overall while its market against your quote asset is quiet. Slippage costs dollars no matter which coin you settle in, so this floor is always in dollars. | text | `500000` | Raise it if auto-added coins are filling at prices noticeably worse than you expected. | This is liquidity on the exact market you would trade — the coin against your quote asset. A popular coin can still have a quiet market against your quote. Raising it shrinks the candidate pool but improves fill quality; too high and discovery finds nothing. |
| `min24hAssetVolumeUsd`<br/>Min 24h volume for the coin (USD) | Is the coin actually alive? The coin's total 24h trading volume on its main US-dollar market, whatever quote asset you happen to trade it against. This is the "no dead microcaps" floor, so set it high. | text | `50000000` | Raise it to keep discovery in genuinely liquid, well-known coins. Lower it only if you deliberately want smaller caps. | This is the "no dead microcaps" floor, measured on the coin's main dollar market rather than yours. It is the single most effective filter against illiquid junk. |
| `maxSpreadRatio`<br/>Max bid/ask spread | Max bid/ask spread as a fraction of mid. 0.003 is 0.3 percent. | text | `0.003` | Tighten it if entries and exits are costing more than the strategy expects. Loosen it if the pool is coming back empty. | You pay roughly half the spread on entry and half on exit, so `0.003` costs about 0.3% per round trip before fees. On a strategy targeting a few percent, that is a real bite. |
| `changeMinPercent`<br/>Min 24h gain (%) | Minimum 24h gain against your quote asset, in percent. 0 means "the coin must simply beat the asset you hold when you are not in a trade" — the one setting here that means the same thing no matter which quote asset you pick. A higher number is a deliberate hurdle, and how hard it is to clear depends on the quote asset. | text | `0` | Raise it above 0 when you only want coins already showing a real move, not merely ones drifting up. | A higher hurdle means far fewer candidates, all of them already up on the day — which also means you are buying later into the move. This is the one filter here whose meaning does not shift when you change quote asset. |
| `rankTopPercent`<br/>Consider top % of gainers | Only consider coins in the top slice of all coins on your quote asset, ranked by 24h gain. 30 means the top 30 percent. Using a rank instead of a fixed percentage is what keeps discovery working when you switch quote asset. | number, min 1, max 100 | `30` | Lower it to be more selective. Raise it if too few coins survive the other filters. | Only coins in the top slice of your quote asset's universe by 24h gain are considered. Because it is a rank and not a fixed percentage, it keeps behaving sensibly when you switch quote asset. |
| `rankExcludeTopPercent`<br/>Skip hottest % of gainers | Skip the very hottest coins, which have usually already run. 5 means ignore the top 5 percent of gainers. Must be smaller than the top-percent setting. 0 skips nothing. | number, min 0, max 99 | `5` | Raise it if auto-added coins are consistently entering right at a local top. | The hottest gainers are skipped, on the theory that they have already run. It must be smaller than the top-percent setting or the window is empty. `0` skips nothing. |
| `minAgeDays`<br/>Min listing age (days) | Minimum kline-history age before a symbol is eligible (max 40, see schema note). | number, min 1, max 40 | `30` | Raise it to avoid freshly listed coins, whose early price action is thin and erratic. Lower it only if you want new listings. | A coin needs this many days of candle history to qualify, which is also what the indicator filters need to compute anything meaningful. Capped at 40 days. |
| `maxAutoSymbols`<br/>Max Auto Symbols | Cap on concurrently auto-held symbols. | number, min 1, max 50 | `5` | Set it from how much capital you have. Each auto-held coin needs enough budget to place an order above the exchange minimum. | Discovery stops adding once this many coins are auto-held. Set too high on a small account and each position is too small to trade; set to 1 and the profile is effectively single-coin. |
| `minHoldMinutes`<br/>Min hold (minutes) | Min hold before reap AND re-add cooldown, in minutes. | number, min 1, max 43200 | `120` | Raise it if coins are being added and dropped repeatedly, churning fees. | Serves double duty: a newly added coin is held at least this long before it can be dropped, and a dropped coin cannot be re-added for the same period. Raising it makes the universe stickier and cuts churn, at the cost of holding a fading coin longer. |
| `marketBreadthMinPercent`<br/>Market Breadth Min Percent | Risk-off guard. Before discovery adds any NEW coin this cycle, at least this percent of all coins in your quote asset must be up over the last 24h. If fewer are up the broad market is bleeding, so no new coins are added (coins you already hold are not touched). 0 turns the guard off. | text | `0` | Set it above 0 when you want discovery to stop adding coins during broad market selloffs. | Before any new coin is added, at least this share of the whole quote-asset universe must be up over 24h. Coins you already hold are never touched by this. Set it high and discovery goes quiet for long stretches; `0` disables the guard. |
| `enterOnAdd`<br/>Enter On Add | Enter on a discovery add. Off (default): a freshly added coin still waits for the strategy buy gate, so a confirmed up-move can sit unbought if the short-interval signal disagrees. On: the first entry skips short-interval confirmation and buys on the 1h momentum discovery already confirmed; the only downside guard left is a Strong-Sell reading. Higher risk, so leave off until a net-of-cost backtest justifies it. | on / off | `false` | Leave off until a net-of-cost backtest justifies it. Turn it on only if you find discovery adds sitting unbought while the move runs away. | Off, a newly added coin still has to pass the strategy's normal buy gate, so it may never be bought. On, the first entry skips short-interval confirmation and buys on the move discovery already confirmed — faster entries, materially higher risk, with only a Strong-Sell reading left as a downside guard. |

**Entry Guard**

| Setting | What it is | Values | Default | When to change it | What to expect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `entryGuard.maxDistanceFrom24hHighPercent`<br/>Max Distance From24h High Percent | Skip a discovery entry while price is within this percent of the 24h high, so the bot does not chase a coin that already ran. 0 turns the guard off. | text | `0` | Set it above 0 if discovery entries keep landing at the top of a spike. | An entry is skipped while price is within this percent of the 24h high. It trades chasing risk for missed entries: on a coin trending cleanly upward, price sits near its 24h high most of the time, so this can block almost everything. |
| `entryGuard.knifeCandles`<br/>Knife Candles | Skip a discovery entry while the last N closed candles are still falling (catching a falling knife). 0 turns the guard off. | number, min 0, max 50 | `0` | Set it above 0 to stop discovery buying into an active collapse. Pair it with the drop-percent setting — both must be non-zero for the guard to bite. | Entry is skipped while the last N closed candles are still falling. A small number (2–3) catches genuine collapses without blocking normal pullbacks. |
| `entryGuard.knifeDropPercent`<br/>Knife Drop Percent | Minimum total drop across the knifeCandles window needed to block the entry. 0 turns the guard off. | text | `0` | Set it alongside knife candles. Raise it so only a serious drop blocks the entry, not any small consecutive decline. | The fall across the knife window must total at least this much for the entry to be blocked. Set very low and every minor dip blocks entry; `0` disables the guard whatever the candle count. |

**Trend Confirm**

| Setting | What it is | Values | Default | When to change it | What to expect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `trendConfirm.adxPeriod`<br/>Adx Period | ADX lookback in candles. | number, min 2, max 100 | `14` | Leave at 14 unless a backtest says otherwise — it is the standard lookback and the reference value below is calibrated to it. | Shortening it makes the trend reading jumpier, so coins qualify and disqualify more often. Lengthening it makes confirmation slower and rarer. |
| `trendConfirm.adxMin`<br/>Adx Min | Minimum ADX for a confirmed trend. 25 is TradingView "trending". | text | `25` | Raise it to demand a stronger, more established trend. Lower it if too few coins ever confirm. | ADX measures trend strength regardless of direction. 25 is the conventional "trending" threshold; above 40 very few coins qualify at any one time. |
| `trendConfirm.emaPeriod`<br/>EMA Period | EMA lookback for the price-above-trend check. | number, min 2, max 400 | `20` | Shorten it to accept coins that have only recently turned up; lengthen it to require a more established uptrend. | Price must sit above this moving average. A long period rejects coins early in a recovery; a short one barely filters at all. |
| `trendConfirm.volSmaPeriod`<br/>Vol SMA Period | Volume-SMA lookback for the participation check. | number, min 2, max 400 | `20` | Leave at the default unless the volume check is behaving oddly on your chosen interval. | Sets the baseline that "unusual volume" is measured against. A short baseline is easily beaten by a single busy candle; a long one is a steadier reference. |
| `trendConfirm.volMultiple`<br/>Vol Multiple | Last volume must exceed this multiple of the volume SMA. | text | `1.5` | Raise it to require real participation behind a move. Lower it if the volume test is rejecting everything. | The latest candle's volume must exceed this multiple of the baseline. At `1.5` a coin needs 50% more volume than typical. Above about 3 only genuine volume spikes qualify. |

**Correlation**

| Setting | What it is | Values | Default | When to change it | What to expect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `correlation.maxPairwise`<br/>Max Pairwise | Max return correlation (0–1) a NEW coin may have with one already held; a more-correlated candidate is skipped so the auto-set is not one beta factor held many times. Lower is stricter; 0.8 blocks near-clones. 0 turns the cap off. | text | `0` | Set it above 0 once discovery is holding several coins, so you are not unknowingly holding the same bet many times. | A new candidate is skipped if it moves too much like something already held. `0.8` blocks near-clones; lower is stricter and produces a genuinely diversified set but far fewer adds. `0` turns the check off, and in a market where most coins move together that means the auto-set is effectively one position. |
| `correlation.lookbackCandles`<br/>Lookback Candles | How many recent candles the correlation is measured over. | number, min 5, max 200 | `30` | Only when the correlation cap is on. Lengthen it for a more stable estimate. | Correlation measured over very few candles is noisy and will let through pairs that are in fact closely linked. A longer window is steadier but slower to notice a relationship changing. |
